disposition_reason: Lead and cadmium by GFAAS in 41 food supplements and plant materials (tinctures, teas, dried fruits, herbal tablets, zeolite and clay powders, omega-3, casein protein) bought in Bucharest in 2018-2019; per-product means and SDs in Table 3.

study.design: Market survey with risk assessment (EDI, THQ, CR)
study.origin: not stated (vegetal, mineral or animal origin per Table 1)
study.market: Drugstores and health food stores, Bucharest, Romania
study.method: 0.5 g microwave digestion with 5 mL HNO3 + 1 mL H2O2, made to 50 mL; GFAAS (AAnalyst 600, Zeeman correction)
lod: Pb LOD 1.2 µg/L, LOQ 3.6 µg/L; Cd LOD 0.2 µg/L, LOQ 0.6 µg/L (in solution); Table 3 non-detects printed as <0.002 mg/kg Pb and <0.0002 mg/kg Cd
study.qa: SRM 3280 in triplicate, recovery above 95% for Pb and Cd

unresolved: Table 3 non-detect thresholds (<0.002 mg/kg Pb, <0.0002 mg/kg Cd) and several reported values (e.g. 0.003 mg/kg Pb) are far below the solution LOD (1.2 µg/L) scaled by the 0.5 g in 50 mL dilution (about 0.12 mg/kg); the per-sample reporting limit is unclear.
Text says the maximum lead was '1274 mg/kg' (SV26); Table 3 gives 1.274 mg/kg.
Tinctures, syrup, hemp oil and some 'liquid' herbal products are reported in mg/kg; density/volume basis not stated.
Table 1 lists 'Shredded linden flowers' and 'Red clover' as 'Liquid in brown glass' and 'Marigold flowers'/'Thyme' as '100 g dried fruit', which may be packaging-column errors.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: EU Regulation 1881/2006 maximum levels for food supplements
regulatory_or_exposure.value: Pb 3.0 mg/kg, Cd 1.0 mg/kg; no sample exceeded

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Estimated daily intake and THQ at maximum label dose (70 kg adult)
regulatory_or_exposure.value: Pb EDI up to 5.460 µg/kg bw/day and THQ 1.820 (SV26); THQ above 1 also for SV29 and SV21; Cd EDI up to 1.143 (SA1)
